profile.summary: Genos is a family of DNA language models for the human genome from the Genos Team in Hangzhou, China (GitHub and Hugging Face organisation BGI-HangzhouAI). It reads DNA one base at a time, with inputs of up to about one million bases, and is trained to predict the next base. Its internal representations (embeddings) are used for tasks such as classifying genomic elements, predicting variant effects and, after fine-tuning, predicting RNA-seq coverage from DNA sequence.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract, Methods; README_en.md: Model Architecture, Notebook Usage Examples

summary_quotes.text: a human-centric genomic foundation model engineered for million-basepair sequence modeling
Each genome sequence was processed using a one-hot tokenizer, with a vocabulary consisting of the 4 canonical nucleotides (A, T, C, G), the undetermined base N, and special tokens
in accordance with the next token prediction (NTP) objective
Ultra-long context: RoPE base 50M, multi-dimensional tensor/pipeline/context/data/expert parallelism; supports up to 1M tokens.
achieving direct prediction of single-base resolution RNA-seq expression profiles from DNA sequences through fine-tuning

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Genos is a decoder-style Transformer with a mixture-of-experts feed-forward layer. Each base (A, T, C, G or N) is one token. Every layer has grouped-query attention, with 16 heads sharing 8 key-value groups, and rotary position embeddings for long contexts; a router sends each token to 2 of 8 expert networks. A final linear layer gives the probability of the next base, which is the training objective. Pre-training mixed sequence lengths of 8,192, 32,768, 131,072 and 1,024,000 bp. For downstream use the paper names three modes: embedding extraction, sequence generation and fine-tuning.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Methods, model architecture, training stages, inference; README_en.md: Model Architecture

quotes.text: Each genome sequence was processed using a one-hot tokenizer
mechanism with 16 attention heads sharing 8 key-value groups
The router dynamically selects 2 of the 8 experts for each token based on sequence content
Transformer-based Mixture of Experts network, Top-2 routing, 25% FFN sparsity.
a linear output layer projects the model’s final hidden state into logits over the vocabulary, where the softmax function then converts them into a probability distribution for the next token
corresponding to sequence lengths of 8,192 bp, 32,768 bp, 131,072 bp, and 1,024,000 bp
The model supports 3 primary modalities: embedding generation, sequence generation, and model fine-tuning.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Three models are released, each as a Hugging Face checkpoint and a Megatron-LM checkpoint: Genos-1.2B and Genos-10B, trained on human genomes, and Genos-10B-v2 (released 2025-12-18), which adds about 60 billion bases of East Asian genomes, non-human primate genomes and other mammalian genomes, mixed 1:1 with the human corpus. Genos-10B-v2 was trained on 6286B tokens against 2200B for Genos-10B, so results from the two are not interchangeable. A result should name the checkpoint and its Hugging Face revision. The README also announces Gengram (2026-01-30) as a separate model in its own repository.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Transformer with mixture-of-experts feed-forward layers (8 experts, top-2 routing), grouped-query attention, rotary position embeddings (RoPE base 50M), 12 layers and 16 attention heads. Genos-1.2B: attention hidden size 1024, expert hidden size 4096. Genos-10B and 10B-v2: 4096 and 8192.

Mixture-of-experts layers keep compute below the total size: 0.33B of 1.2B parameters, or 2.87B of 10B, are active per token.
Training data reflect human diversity through pangenome assemblies from HPRC, HGSVC and CEPH rather than one reference genome.

run_guide.summary: Start the Genos Docker image, place the Genos-1.2B weights locally and print per-layer embeddings for a random 8,192-base sequence.
prerequisites: Docker with GPU support: the README runs the image with --gpus all.
A CUDA GPU that supports bfloat16 and FlashAttention 2, as the notebook loads the model that way. Memory needs are not stated.
The Genos-1.2B weights from https://huggingface.co/BGI-HangzhouAI/Genos-1.2B. The licence is stated as Apache 2.0 in the README and MIT in the Hugging Face metadata.

steps.title: Extract embeddings
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer

# Specify model path
model_path = "/path/to/your/local/Genos-1.2B" # Replace with local model path

# Load tokenizer and model
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_path)

# Load locally downloaded Genos weights
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_path,
                                  output_hidden_states=True,
                                  torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
                                  trust_remote_code=True,
                                  attn_implementation="flash_attention_2" # Use flash_attention
  )
model.cuda() # Load model to GPU
model.eval() # Switch model to inference mode

import random

# Randomly select a specific number of bases
bases = ['A', 'T', 'G', 'C']
seqs = random.choices(bases, k=8192)
# Generate input base sequence
text = ''.join(seqs)

# Encode text
inputs = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt")

# Load data to GPU
inputs = {k: v.cuda() for k, v in inputs.items()}

# Model inference
with torch.no_grad():
    outputs = model(**inputs)

# Get hidden states from all layers
hidden_states = outputs.hidden_states  # Tuple containing hidden states from each layer

# Iterate through embeddings from each layer and display key information
for i, layer_embedding in enumerate(hidden_states):
    print(f"Layer {i} embedding ({layer_embedding.shape}): {layer_embedding[0, 0, :10]}")
    print("-" * 50)
PY

notes: The record is attached to ViroBench (viral genomics), which evaluated a model labelled 'Genos'; which checkpoint it used was not checked. BGI-HangzhouAI also publishes Genos-m on Hugging Face, tagged microbe and metagenomics, which the README read does not mention; it may be the checkpoint relevant to a viral benchmark and may deserve its own record.
